scope: Independent requested-byte/count backing admission for device namespace and MMIO/IRQ/DMA capability payload nodes, through empty candidates, published descriptors and complete detached/retired owners.
artifact_note: Runtime sources were frozen before the campaigns. Every manifest tracked-diff identity equals the final runtime patch. Documentation/evidence edits followed manifest preparation; new source identities are included explicitly.

dimensions: actual requested retirement-node layout bytes including charge and inline payload storage
policy.decision: Twice existing unified-capability ceilings plus the root-metadata complete-root planning envelope: 2*(49152+3072) ordinary and 2*(65536+4096) total. Candidate/replacement/retirement headroom preserves existing resource limits; independent byte ceilings permit layout growth. No RAM preallocation.
policy.cost: 16 extra bytes per node (2176 KiB at total count ceiling), an independent short admission/refund operation and an existing ResourceLimit rejection. No extra holder allocation, runtime registry or cleanup family.
policy.classification: Capture root generation and table-account backing classification under one table hold, then acquire that exact AddressSpaceOperation before node allocation. A retirement/reuse race rejects lease acquisition. Permanent kernel storage is trusted. Original class survives promotion, detachment and retirement; allocator/release never re-resolves ASID. Resource grants stay separate.
policy.rejection: Each node quota rejection precedes its own heap allocation. First/second node failure publishes no authority, hardware/reset work or descriptor. A partial two-node preparation disposes original unused storage before exact-root completion, outside local publication guards.
policy.release: Typed DeviceMap/Prepared/Retired nodes carry original backing through existing GrantAdmission, PreparedClose, DmaOperation and PreparedNamespaceDevices. Actual node deallocation precedes refund. Existing complete fallback retains nodes/authority/root without entering the pool; hardware uncertainty never authorizes refund or replay.
policy.exclusions: IOMMU backend domain/requester/context, mapping/walker and table-ledger storage, nested allocations, allocator bookkeeping and aggregate principal/general-heap accounting remain separate.

controls: Actual mixed empty namespace/capability-layout candidates fill ordinary 104448 and total 139264 ceilings. The additional 104447 ordinary and 34815 trusted candidates reflect the two pre-existing root namespaces, not lower limits.

With the real heap held, 64 ordinary and 64 trusted rounds reject both individual layouts (256 denials) and the complete two-node storage constructor (128 denials). All three actual MMIO/IRQ/DMA grant adapters reject 32 times at ordinary exhaustion, and for both roots at total exhaustion (288 adapter denials), with original node/authority/device state and route ownership unchanged.

One available ordinary slot runs all three adapters 32 times (96 denials) and one extra complete-storage rejection. First-node allocation succeeds, second-node admission rejects and the original partial candidate recovers exactly. Two slots permit real MMIO grant/close; promotion cannot redirect its original ordinary refund. Exact two-kind refill restores full admission.

Trusted real MMIO grant/close and complete grant preparation/cancellation progress at ordinary backing exhaustion. Unified capability resource counters remain ordinary, proving that trusted metadata backing alone grants no platform resource admission.

Two concrete layouts each inject 64 node-allocator rejections (128 total), recovering original byte/count reservations. Oversized inline layout types independently reject ordinary/total bytes before entering the allocation callback, without constructing those payloads.

Original empty two-node storage outlives actual root close and exact numeric ASID reuse by a trusted successor; later explicit disposal refunds only the original ordinary bytes/count. Empty candidates have no device authority, mapping or hardware obligation.

Existing real device/unified publication and explicit MMIO/IRQ claim fixtures also hold the node pool guard. Scratch/direct mapped MMIO and IRQ close retain original node charges through cleanup and recover exactly after staged root completion.

Existing complete DMA grant, backend-metadata grant, explicit-close and namespace abandonment fixtures add the node pool guard to their existing holds. Their original authority, roots, scratch and hardware obligations remain retained; no extra deliberate-retention owner is introduced. Existing native NVMe/reset/map/unmap recovery fixtures execute unchanged.

Shared retirement-collection host controls establish payload disposal and actual node deallocation before charge refund, allocation-error rollback and inert detached-node fallback. Backing admission does not supply hardware completion or broader caller-context qualification.
qualification_limits: Serialized kernel-fixture pressure, not sustained concurrent hostile EL0 fairness or forced native general heap OOM. Byte rejection uses oversized layout admission, not real byte-ceiling allocations; node allocation failures are injected.

Empty-candidate ASID reuse is backing-lifetime qualification, not physical MMIO/DMA retirement. Existing mapped MMIO and NVMe tests retain their narrower reset/completion contracts; no outstanding device I/O or new hardware timeout is injected.

IOMMU backend registry, per-domain mapping/walker and table-ledger backing still need independent admission. Other registry/control storage, allocator bookkeeping, all-family signed-principal admission, general heap and worst-case latency remain open.

No new reserve grant, lease kind, physical completion proof, retry/replay owner, cleanup registry or owner family. SEC-07 remains partial; C12/C13/C14 and wider G1/G4/essential-progress gates remain applicable.
